fiscal_year_note: FILENAME MISMATCH — CRITICAL: the PDF is named 'Dropbox10k2025.pdf' but the filing covers FISCAL YEAR 2024 (ended December 31, 2024), filed February 2025. All ground-truth values here are FY2024.
reporting_unit_warning: Dropbox reports in MILLIONS with ONE DECIMAL PLACE (e.g. 2,548.2). Truncating the decimal loses precision that the filing actually provides.

accrued_amount.note: No aggregate legal accrual figure disclosed.

reasonably_possible_loss_in_excess_of_ac.note: Dropbox provides its accrual policy (record a liability when probable and estimable) for ordinary-course claims. No 'reasonably possible' loss quantification was located.

legal_contingencies.verbatim_quote: From time-to-time, the Company is a party to a variety of claims, lawsuits, investigations, inquiries, and proceedings which arise in the ordinary course of business, including claims of alleged infringement of intellectual property rights, regulatory matters, and commercial disputes. The Company records a liability when it believes that it is probable that a loss will be incurred and the amount of loss or range of loss can be reasonably estimated.

individual_matters.note: No individually quantified legal matters extracted.

segment_reporting.segment_basis: Single operating and reportable segment; geographic revenue disaggregation only
segment_reporting.segment_statement_verbatim: The Company's chief operating decision-maker (“CODM”), the Chief Executive Officer, manages the Company's business activities as a single operating and reportable segment at the consolidated level.
segment_reporting.profit_measure: Consolidated net income (CODM uses consolidated measures); no per-segment profit measure exists
segment_reporting.geographic_note: No single country outside the United States accounted for more than 10% of total revenue.
traps: There is NO segment operating income to extract — a single-segment filer. An extractor must report 'single reportable segment', not fabricate segment profit lines.
The US/International split is a GEOGRAPHIC disaggregation, not segment reporting.
A separate long-lived-assets-by-geography table (line 2258: United States $353.1) uses the same 'United States' row label and can be mistaken for revenue.
Amounts carry one decimal place in millions.

income_taxes.provision_sign_convention: The reconciliation table uses NEGATIVE-IN-PARENTHESES = TAX EXPENSE. The FY2024 bottom line prints as $(57.5) on a row labeled '(Provision for) benefit from income taxes', which is a PROVISION (expense) of $57.5 million — NOT a tax benefit.
income_taxes.effective_tax_rate_note: COMPUTED, not printed. Dropbox's reconciliation table shows DOLLARS ONLY with no percent column and no effective-tax-rate line. 57.5 / 509.8 = 11.28%. Cross-check against the statutory line: 107.1 / 0.21 = 510.0 ≈ 509.8 pretax ✓.
income_taxes.reconciliation_presentation: dollars only (no percent column, no ETR line), three years (2024, 2023, 2022)

rate_reconciliation_fy2024.line: Provision for income taxes at federal statutory rate
State taxes, net of federal benefit

fy2022.note: FY2022 was a genuine net BENEFIT of $360.5M, driven by a $409.9M valuation-allowance release — the sign genuinely flips between years.

unrecognized_tax_benefits.verbatim_quote: As of December 31, 2024, the balance of unrecognized tax benefits was $162.7 million of which $114.6 million, if recognized, would affect the effective tax rate and $48.1 million would result in adjustment to deferred tax assets with corresponding adjustments to the valuation allowance.

traps: SIGN TRAP (highest risk in this filing): $(57.5) is a tax EXPENSE, not a benefit. The row label '(Provision for) benefit from income taxes' invites the wrong reading, and FY2022's +360.5 really is a benefit, so the sign is not constant across columns.

No effective tax rate is printed anywhere in the reconciliation — it must be computed as 57.5 / 509.8 = 11.3%. Reporting 'not disclosed' is defensible only if the derivation is not attempted; reporting 21.0% (statutory) as the ETR is wrong.
$162.7M gross UTB vs $114.6M ETR-affecting — the $48.1M difference is valuation-allowance offset.
